newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S PARREIRA TO COACH MSL'S METROSTARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S PARREIRA TO COACH MSL'S METROSTARS.

text.p: Carlos Alberto Parreira, who steered Brazil to a record fourth World Cup title in 1994, signed a two-year contract Monday to coach the New York/New Jersey MetroStars of Major League Soccer.
Parriera was termed a "perfect fit" for the fledgling franchise by general manager Charlie Stillitano.
"I don't think there is a coach in the world who is better equipped for this job," said Stillitano. "It was paramount to the MetroStars that Carlos sign a two-year contract.
"He is making a commitment to the organisation, our players and most of all, our fans."
Parreira, 53, becomes the third coach in the brief history of the team, following Eddie Firmani and Carlos Queiroz.

Firmani, the last coach of the long-defunct New York Cosmos, hastily left the team after posting a 3-5 record, and Queiroz, the former Portuguese national team coach, finished the season but left to take a lucrative offer with the Grampus Eight of Japan's J-League.

Parriera has been a presense in international competition for more than a decade. He coached Kuwait to the World Cup in 1982 and led the United Arab Emirates into the 1990 World Cup. During two stints with the Brazilian national team, Parriera posted a 28-5-13 record in international competition, including a perfect run during the 1994 World Cup.
Since the World Cup, Parriera has coached Seville of the Spanish League and led Fenerbahce to the Turkish League title. He coached PC Sao Paulo in the Brazilian League this past season.
